adopted: Protected routes admit only a BFF-verified browser session whose strict BFF-owned authReady signal is true.
Provider readiness is not an authentication decision: an auth-ready session remains admitted when providerReady is false or a later provider verification reports an error.
A re-verification failure for the same GCP Identity user retains a previously strict BFF session instead of clearing its in-memory bearer bridge.
The combined BFF /me and /bff/auth/readiness verification is aborted after 5000 ms, so a provider-related stall cannot leave the route guard loading indefinitely.
not_changed: The AGORA-AGC-01-AUTH-BFF-20260827 server contract, server-side authorization, roles, capabilities, or real-write policy.
Firebase/GCP Identity authentication, browser credential persistence, tenant-claim selection, sign-out semantics, or auth return-target validation.
Provider-dependent feature gates, which continue to decide availability separately from protected-route admission.

security_boundaries.authoritative_admission: Only a strict BFF readback with authReady=true admits a protected route. Firebase identity alone, a missing BFF session, and authReady=false still redirect to the applicable auth route.
security_boundaries.provider_isolation: providerReady is deliberately excluded from the route decision. A provider outage cannot discard a previously verified same-user session or turn it into a login redirect.
security_boundaries.timeout_behavior: The timeout aborts the in-flight BFF requests rather than weakening authentication. With no previous auth-ready BFF session, the route remains fail closed after the bounded verification error.
security_boundaries.credential_storage: No persistent bearer or browser-editable authorization state is introduced; the existing in-memory Firebase-to-BFF header provider remains the sole bearer bridge.
